children.translated_text: Now, therefore, the procedure for the household cooked oblations.

children.text: parisamuhyopalipyollikhyoddhṛtyābhyukṣyāgnimupasamādhāya dakṣiṇato brahmāsanamāstīrya praṇīya paristīryārthavadāsādya pavitre kṛtvā prokṣaṇīḥ saṃskṛtyārthavatprokṣya nirupyājyamadhiśritya paryagni kuryāt
children.translated_text: Having swept around, smeared, drawn lines, lifted out the earth, sprinkled, and set down the fire, he should spread the seat for the <s>brahman</s> priest to the south, bring forward the water, spread around, set down what is needed with the proper formulas, make the two purifiers, prepare the sprinkling waters, sprinkle what is needed with the proper formulas, take out the ghee, place it on the fire, and carry fire around it.

children.text: sruvaṃ pratapya sammṛjyābhyukṣya punaḥ pratapya nidadhyāt
children.translated_text: He should heat the ladle, wipe it, sprinkle it, heat it again, and set it down.

children.text: ājyamudvāsyotpūyāvekṣya prokṣaṇīśca pūrvavadupayamanānkuśānādāya samidho 'bhyādhāya paryukṣya juhuyāt
children.translated_text: Having taken down the ghee, purified it, inspected it, and likewise the sprinkling waters, he should take the handfuls of kuśa grass for touching, put on the fuel-sticks, sprinkle around, and make the oblation.
This very rule applies wherever there is a homa.
The establishment of the householder's fire is at the time of marriage.
According to some, it is at the time of division of inheritance.
For a Vaiśya rich in cattle, the fire is brought from his own house.
Everything is as in the cooking of the cātuṣprāśya.
Some prescribe the handing over of the fire-drill.
Because scripture says, 'the five great sacrifices.'
Having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> for the deities of the fire-establishment, he offers the two portions of ghee and the ghee-oblations on either side.

children.text: tvanno 'gne satvanno 'gna imammevaruṇa tatvāyāmi ye te śatamayāścāgna uduttamaṃ bhavatanna ityaṣūau purastāt
children.translated_text: The eight formulas beginning 'From you, O Agni,' 'Through you, O Agni,' 'This, O Varuṇa,' 'For that I approach you,' 'Those hundredfold medicines of yours,' 'And, O Agni,' 'Upmost,' and 'Be for us' are used beforehand.
In the same way, after offering from above the cooked oblation to the deities of the fire-establishment, he offers.
And to <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.

children.text: ayāsyagnervaṣaū kṛtaṃ yatkarmaṇātyarīricaṃ devāgātu vida iti
children.translated_text: With the formula, 'What has been made by this offering of Agni, what through the rite has been exceeded; the gods have gone to the knower.'
Having offered the sacred grass, he eats.
After that comes the feeding of Brahmins.

children.text: ṣaḍarghyā bhavantyācārya ṛtvigvaivāhyo rājā priyaḥ snātaka iti
children.translated_text: There are six persons worthy of an arghya: the teacher, the officiating priest, the bridegroom, the king, a dear guest, and a snātaka.
They should honor them every year.
But officiating priests when they are about to sacrifice.
Having brought a seat, he says, 'Let your honor sit down; we shall honor your honor.'

children.text: āharanti viṣūaraṃ padyaṃ pādārthamudakamarghamācamanīyaṃ madhuparkaṃ dadhimadhughṛtamapihitaṃ kāṃsye kāṃsyena
children.translated_text: They bring a grass-seat, foot-water, water for washing the feet, an arghya, water for sipping, and the madhuparka: curds, honey, and ghee, covered in a bronze vessel with a bronze lid.
Another person says three times, 'The grass-seat and the rest.'
He receives the grass-seat.

children.text: varṣmo 'smi samānānāmudyatāmiva sūryaḥ \ imaṃ tamabhitiṣūhāmi yo mā kaścābhidāsatītyenamabhyupaviśati
children.translated_text: With 'I am the highest among my peers, like the risen sun; I tread upon him, whoever plots against me,' he sits upon it.
Another grass-seat is placed at the feet for him as he sits.
After washing the left foot, he washes the right.
If he is a Brahmin, the right foot is washed first.

children.text: virājo doho 'si virājo dohamaśīya mayi pādyāyai virājo doha iti
children.translated_text: With the formula, 'You are the milking of <s>Virāj</s>; may I obtain the milking of <s>Virāj</s>; in me, for the foot-water, is the milking of <s>Virāj</s>.'
He receives the arghya with, 'You are waters; through you may I obtain all desires.'

children.text: ninayannabhimantrayate samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomi svāṃ yonimabhigacchata \ ariṣūā asmākaṃ vīrā mā parāsecimatpaya iti
children.translated_text: As he pours it away, he addresses it: 'I send you to the ocean; go to your own womb. Let our heroes be unharmed; do not pour away our vigor.'

children.text: ācāmatyāmāganyaśasā saṃsṛja varcasā \ taṃ mā kuru priyaṃ prajānāmadhipatiṃ paśūnāmariṣūiṃ tanūnāmiti
children.translated_text: He sips, saying, 'Come to me together with fame, with splendor. Make me dear to creatures, lord of cattle, and unharmed in my bodies.'
With 'Of <s>Mitra</s> you are,' he looks at the madhuparka.
With 'Of the god you are,' he receives it.

children.text: savye pāṇau kṛtvā dakṣiṇasyānāmikayā triḥ prayauti namaḥ śyāvāsyāyānnaśane yatta āviddhaṃ tatte niṣkṛntāmīti
children.translated_text: Having placed it in the left hand, with the ring finger of the right he stirs it three times, saying, 'Homage to the dark one, the eater of food; whatever in you is pierced, may that be cut out for you.'
And with the ring finger and thumb he wipes it out three times.

children.text: tasya triḥ prāśnāti yanmadhuno madhavyaṃ paramaṃ rūpamannādyam \ tenāhaṃ madhuno madhavyena parameṇa rūpeṇānnādyena paramo madhavyo 'nnādo 'sānīti
children.translated_text: He eats from it three times, saying, 'Whatever is honeyed in the honey, the highest form, fit for food: through that honeyedness of honey, through that highest form fit for food, may I become supremely honeyed and an eater of food.'
Or he may do so with each verse of the Madhumatī verses.
He should give the remainder to his son or to his pupil seated to the north.
Or he may eat it all.
Or he may pour it out in an eastward passage.

children.text: ācamya prāṇāntsaṃmṛśati vā￦ma āsye nasoḥ prāṇo 'kṣṇoścakṣuḥ karṇayoḥ śrotraṃ bāhvorbalamūrvorojo 'riṣūāni me '￦gāni tanūstanvā me saheti
children.translated_text: After sipping, he touches the vital parts: 'Speech in my mouth, breath in the nostrils, sight in the eyes, hearing in the ears, strength in the arms, vigor in the thighs; may my limbs be unharmed, my body together with my body.'
To him who has sipped water, taking up the command, he says three times, 'A cow.'

children.text: pratyāha \ mātā rudrāṇāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ svasādityānāmamṛtasya nābhiḥ \ pranuvocañcikituṣe janāya māgāmanāgāmaditiṃ vadhiṣūa \ mama cāmuṣya ca pāpmānaṃ hanomīti yadyālabheta
children.translated_text: He replies: 'Mother of the <s>Rudras</s>, daughter of the <s>Vasus</s>, sister of the <s>Ādityas</s>, navel of immortality: speak forth to the discerning people; do not kill the guiltless cow, <s>Aditi</s>. I strike down my sin and that of this man,' if he should touch it.

children.text: atha yadyutsisṛkṣenmama cāmuṣya ca pāpmā hata omutsṛjata tṛṇānyattviti brūyāt
children.translated_text: But if he wishes to release it, he should say, 'My sin and that of this man has been struck down. Om, release it; let it eat grass.'
Yet the arghya should not be without meat.
He should simply say, 'He performs it in connection with a sacrifice and in connection with a marriage.'

children.text: yadyapyasakṛtsaṃvatsarasya somena yajeta kṛtārghyā evainaṃ yājayeyurnākṛtārghyā iti śruteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even if he were to sacrifice with Soma more than once in a year, only those who have received the arghya should make him sacrifice, not those who have not received the arghya, according to scripture.

children.text: catvāraḥ pākayajñā huto 'hutaḥ prahutaḥ prāśita iti
children.translated_text: There are four pākayajñas: offered, unoffered, offered forth, and eaten.

children.text: pañcasu bahiḥśālāyāṃ vivāhe cūḍākaraṇa upanayane keśānte sīmantonnayana iti
children.translated_text: In five rites it is outside the hall: marriage, tonsure, initiation, first beard-shaving, and parting of the pregnant woman's hair.
On a place that has been smeared, from which the loose earth has been removed, and which has been sprinkled, he sets down the fire.
Some prescribe a newly churned fire at marriage.

children.text: udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇyāhe kumāryāḥ pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīyāt
children.translated_text: In the northward course of the sun, in the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious day, he should take the maiden's hand.
In the three sets of three nakṣatras beginning with Uttarā.
Or under <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, or <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
For a Brahmin there are three wives, in the order of the classes.
For a Kṣatriya there are two.
For a Vaiśya there is one.
Some allow a Śūdra woman also for all, but without mantras.

children.text: athaināṃ vāsaḥ paridhāpayati jarāṃ gaccha paridhatsva vāso bhavākṛṣūīnāmabhiśastipāvā \ śataṃ ca jīva śaradaḥ suvarccā rayiṃ ca putrānanusaṃvyayasvāyuṣmatīdaṃ paridhatsva vāsa iti
children.translated_text: Then he makes her put on a garment, saying, 'Go to old age; put on the garment. Be a warder-off of harmful spells. Live a hundred autumns, bright with splendor, and wrap yourself in wealth and sons. Long-lived, put on this garment.'

children.text: athottarīyam \ yā akṛntannavayaṃ yā atanvata \ yāśca devīstantūnabhito tatantha \ tāstvā devīrjarase saṃvyayasvāyuṣmatīdaṃ paridhatsva vāsa iti
children.translated_text: Then the upper garment: "The goddesses who cut, who wove, who stretched the threads all around, may those goddesses clothe you for old age. Put on this garment, rich in life."

children.text: athainau samañjayati \ samañjantu viśvedevāḥ samāpo hṛdayāni nau \ saṃmātariśvā saṃdhātā samudeṣūrī dadhātu nāviti
children.translated_text: Then he anoints the two of them together: "May all the gods unite us; may the waters unite our hearts. May <s>Mātariśvan</s>, the establisher, and the impeller unite us two."

children.text: pitrā prattāmādāya gṛhītvā niṣkāmati \ yadaiṣi manasā dūraṃ diśo 'nu pavamāno vā \ hiraṇyaparṇo vaikarṇaḥ sa tvā manmanasāṃ karotvityasāviti
children.translated_text: Having taken her when she has been given by her father, he goes out holding her: "When you go far away in mind, following the directions, like the purifying wind, may the golden-winged, broad-eared one make you of my mind, O so-and-so."

children.text: athainau samīkṣayati \ aghoracakṣurapatighnyedhi śivā paśubhyaḥ sumanāḥ suvarccāḥ \ vīrasūrddevakāmāsyonāśanno bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade \ somaḥ prathamo vivide gandharvo vivida uttaraḥ \ tṛtīyo 'gniṣūe patisturīyaste manuṣyajāḥ \ somo 'dadadgandharvāya gandharvo 'dadagnaye \ rayiṃ ca putrāścādādagnirmahyamatho imām \ sā naḥ pūṣā śivatamāmairaya sā na ūrū uśatī vihara \ yasyāmuśantaḥ praharāma śepaṃ yasyāmu kāmā bahavo niviṣūyā iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he looks at the two of them together: "Be one whose eye is not terrible, not hostile to your husband; be auspicious for the cattle, kindly, splendid. Be a mother of heroes, dear to the gods; be gracious to our people, bringing welfare to biped and quadruped. <s>Soma</s> first won her; the <s>Gandharva</s> won her next. As third, <s>Agni</s> was your husband; as fourth are men born of <s>Manu</s>. <s>Soma</s> gave her to the <s>Gandharva</s>; the <s>Gandharva</s> gave her to <s>Agni</s>. <s>Agni</s> gave wealth and sons, and then gave this woman to me. May <s>Pūṣan</s> send her to us as most auspicious; may she, eager, open her thighs for us, she in whom, eager, we thrust the male member, she in whom many desires are settled."
Some lead them around the fire clockwise.
Behind the fire he sits down after first moving a reed or mat with his right foot.

children.text: anvārabdha āghārāvājyabhāgau mahāvyāhṛtayaḥ sarvaprāyaścittaṃ prājāpatyaṃ sviṣūakṛcca
children.translated_text: While she is holding on to him, there are the two <s>āghāra</s> offerings, the two portions of ghee, the great utterances, the universal expiation, the <s>Prājāpatya</s> offering, and the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> offering.
This is constant everywhere.
If there is an oblation of ghee other than the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, it is before the great utterances.
In a wedding this insertion has its place between the universal expiation and the <s>Prājāpatya</s>.
One desiring the <s>rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> offerings should know the <s>jaya</s> and <s>abhyātāna</s> formulas.
Because of the statement, "by whatever rite he may desire."

children.text: cittaṃ ca cittiścākūtaṃ cākūtiśca vijñātaṃ ca vijñātiśca manaśca śakvarīśca darśaśca paurṇamāsaṃ ca bṛhacca rathantaraṃ ca \ prajāpatirjayānindrāya vṛṣṇe prāyacchadugraḥ pṛtanā jayeṣu \ tasmai viśaḥ samanamanta sarvāḥ sa ugraḥ sa ihavyo babhūva svāheti
children.translated_text: "Thought and thinking, intention and intending, what is known and knowing, mind and the <s>Śakvarī</s>, the new-moon and full-moon rites, the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>: <s>Prajāpati</s> gave the victories to mighty <s>Indra</s> in the winning of battles. To him all peoples bowed together; he, the mighty one, became worthy of invocation here. Svāhā."

children.text: agnirbhūtānāmadhipatiḥ samāvatvindro jyeṣūhānāṃ yamaḥ pṛthivyā vāyurantarikṣasya sūryo divaścandramā nakṣatrāṇāṃ bṛhaspatirbrahmaṇo mitraḥ satyānāṃ varuṇo 'pāṃ samudraḥ srotyānāmannaṃ sāmrājyānāmadhipati tanmāvatu soma oṣadhīnāṃ savitā prasavānāṃ rudraḥ paśūnāṃ tvaṣūā rūpāṇāṃ viṣṇuḥ parvatānāṃ maruto gaṇānāmadhipatayaste māvantu pitaraḥ pitāmahāḥ parevare tatāstatāmahāḥ \ iha māvantvasminbrahmaṇyasmin kṣatre 'syāmāśiṣyasyāṃ purodhāyāmasminkarmaṇyasyāṃ devahūtyāṃ svāheti sarvatrānuṣajati
children.translated_text: "May <s>Agni</s>, lord of beings, protect me; <s>Indra</s> of the eldest, <s>Yama</s> of the earth, <s>Vāyu</s> of the atmosphere, <s>Sūrya</s> of heaven, the moon of the constellations, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> of sacred speech, <s>Mitra</s> of truths, <s>Varuṇa</s> of the waters, the ocean of streams, and food, lord of sovereignties, protect me. May <s>Soma</s> of the plants, <s>Savitṛ</s> of impellings, <s>Rudra</s> of cattle, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> of forms, <s>Viṣṇu</s> of mountains, and the <s>Maruts</s>, lords of troops, protect me. May the fathers, grandfathers, the nearer and farther ancestors, protect me here, in this priestly power, in this royal power, in this blessing, in this priestly office, in this rite, in this invocation of the gods. Svāhā." He appends this everywhere.

children.text: agniraitu prathamo devatānāṃ so 'syai prajāṃ muñcatu mṛtyupāśāt \ tadayaṃ rājā varuṇo 'numanyatāṃ yatheyaṃ strī pautramaghannarodātsvāhā \ imāmagnistraāyatā￦gārhapatyaḥ prajāmasyai nayatu dīrghamāyuḥ \ aśūnyopasthā jīvatāmastu mātā pautramānandamabhivibudhyatāmiyaṃ svāhā \ svastino agne diva āpṛthivyā viśvānidhehyayathā yajatra yadasyāṃ mahidivi jātaṃ praśastaṃ tadasmāsu draviṇaṃ dhehi citraṃ svāhā \ sugannu panthāṃ pradiśanna ehi jyotiṣmadhye hyajaranna āyuḥ \ apaitu mṛtyuramṛtanna āgādvaivasvato no abhayaṃ kṛṇotu svāheti
children.translated_text: "Let <s>Agni</s> come first among the deities; let him release her offspring from the noose of death. Let this king <s>Varuṇa</s> approve, so that this woman may not weep over the death of a grandson. Svāhā. May this <s>Gārhapatya</s> <s>Agni</s> protect her; may he lead offspring for her and long life. May the mother have an unwasted lap and live; may she awake to joy in a grandson. Svāhā. O <s>Agni</s>, place welfare for us from heaven and earth; O worshipful one, set in us all the splendid wealth that has been born in her, in the great heaven. Svāhā. Come to us, showing the good path; lead us to light and undecaying life. Let death depart; immortality has come to us. May <s>Vaivasvata</s> make fearlessness for us. Svāhā."
Some add "let death go away" at the end of the eating.
The maiden's brother pours parched grain mixed with leaves of <s>śamī</s> and <s>palāśa</s> from his cupped hands into her cupped hands.

children.text: tāñjuhoti saṃhatena tiṣūhatī aryamaṇaṃ devaṃ kanyāgnimayakṣata \ sano aryamā devaḥ preto muñcatu mā pateḥ svāhā \ iyaṃ nāryupabrūte lājānāvapantikā \ āyuṣmānastu me patiredhantāṃ jñātayo mama svāhā \ imā￢llājānāvapāmyagnau samṛddhikaraṇaṃ tava \ mama tubhya ca saṃvananaṃ tadagniranumanyatāmiyaṃ svāheti
children.translated_text: She offers them while standing with joined hands: "The maiden has sacrificed to god <s>Aryaman</s>, and to <s>Agni</s>. May that god <s>Aryaman</s>, once invoked, release us, but not from the husband. Svāhā. This woman declares as she pours the parched grains: may my husband be long-lived; may my kinsmen prosper. Svāhā. I pour these parched grains into the fire for your prosperity. May there be concord between me and you; may <s>Agni</s> approve this. Svāhā."

children.text: athāsyai dakṣiṇaṃ hastam gṛhṇāti sā￦guṣūhaṃ gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ mayāpatyā jaradaṣūiryathā saḥ \ bhago ' 'ryamā savitā purandhirmahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya devāḥ \ amo 'hamasmi sā tvaṃ sā tvamasyamo 'ham \ sāmāhamasmi ṛktvaṃ dyaurahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ tāvehi vivahāvahai sahareto dadhāvahai prajāṃ prajanayāvahai putrānvindyāvahai bahūn te santu jaradaṣūayaḥ saṃpriyau rociṣṇū sumanasyamānau paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ śataṃ śṛṇuyāma śaradaḥ śatamiti ||
children.translated_text: Then he takes her right hand, with the thumb: "I take your hand for good fortune, so that, with me as husband, you may reach old age. <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, and <s>Purandhi</s>, the gods, have given you to me for householdership. I am he; you are she. You are she; I am he. I am the <s>Sāman</s>; you are the <s>Ṛc</s>. I am heaven; you are earth. Come, let us two marry; let us hold seed together; let us beget offspring; let us obtain many sons. May they live to old age. May we, dear to each other, radiant, and of good mind, see a hundred autumns, live a hundred autumns, and hear a hundred autumns."

children.text: athaināmaśmānamārohayatyuttarato 'gnerdakṣiṇapādena ārohemamaśmānamaśmeva tvaṃ sthirā bhava \ abhitiṣūha pṛtanyato 'vabādhasva pṛtanāyata iti
children.translated_text: Then, north of the fire, he makes her step on a stone with her right foot: "Step upon this stone; be firm like a stone. Stand against those who attack; drive away those who fight against you."

children.text: atha gāthāṃ gāyati sarasvati predamava subhage vājinīvatī \ yāṃ tvā viśvasya bhūtasya prajāyāmasyāgrataḥ \ yasyāṃ bhūtaṃ samabhavadyasyāṃ viśvamidaṃ jagat \ tāmadya gāthāṃ gāsyāmi yā strīṇāmuttamaṃ yaśa iti
children.translated_text: Then he sings a verse: "<s>Sarasvatī</s>, come forward here, fortunate one, rich in strength: you whom, at the beginning, the offspring of every being held foremost; in whom what has come into being arose, in whom this whole world exists. Today I shall sing that verse of yours, which is the highest renown of women."

children.text: atha parikrāmataḥ tubhyamagre paryavahansūryāṃ vahatu nā saha \ punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṃ dāgne prajayā saheti
children.translated_text: Then, as they go around, he says: "For you they first led <s>Sūryā</s> around; let the carrying be together with us. O <s>Agni</s>, bring the wife back to her husbands together with offspring."
In this way the other two rounds are performed, beginning with the parched-grain offering.
For the fourth time, with a winnowing basket, he pours all the parched grain into the hollow, saying, "To <s>Bhaga</s>, svāhā."
When she has been led around three times, he offers the <s>Prājāpatya</s> oblation.

children.text: athaināmudīcīṃ saptapadāni prakrāmayati ekamiṣe dve ūrje trīṇi rāyaspoṣāya catvāri māyobhavāya pañca paśubhyaḥ ṣaḍ ṛtubhyaḥ sakhe saptapadā bhava sā māmanuvratā bhava
children.translated_text: Then he makes her step seven steps toward the north: "One for food, two for strength, three for prosperity in wealth, four for well-being, five for cattle, six for the seasons. Be my friend of seven steps. Be one who follows my vow."
Everywhere he adds, "May <s>Viṣṇu</s> lead you."

children.text: niṣkramaṇaprabhṛtyudakumbhaṃ skandhe kṛtvā dakṣiṇato 'gnervāgyataḥ sthito bhavati
children.translated_text: From the time of going out onward, having placed a water jar on his shoulder, he stands silently to the south of the fire.
According to some, he stands to the north.

children.text: tata enāṃ mūrddhanyabhiṣiñcati āpaḥ śivāḥ śivatamāḥ śāntāḥ śāntatamāstāste kṛṇvantu bheṣajamiti
children.translated_text: Then he sprinkles her on the head: "The waters are auspicious, most auspicious, peaceful, most peaceful. May they make medicine for you."
And with the three verses beginning "The waters indeed..."
Then he makes her look up at the sun, with the verse beginning "That eye..."

children.text: athāsyai dakṣiṇāṃ samadhihṛdayamālabhate mama vrate te hṛdayaṃ dadhāmi mama cittamanucittaṃ te astu mama vācamekamanā juṣasva prajāpatiṣūvā niyunaktu mahyamiti

children.translated_text: For a brāhmaṇa the ending is <s>śarman</s>, for a kṣatriya <s>varman</s>, and for a vaiśya <s>gupta</s>.
In the fourth month is the niṣkramaṇikā, the first taking out.
He has him look up at the sun with the verse beginning, "That eye."
When he returns from abroad, he approaches the household as before.

children.text: putraṃ dṛṣūvā japati a￦gāda￦gātsaṃbhavasi hṛdayādadhijāyase \ ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatamiti
children.translated_text: Seeing his son, he murmurs: "From limb after limb you arise; from the heart you are born. You are indeed the self under the name of son; live a hundred autumns."

children.text: athāsya mūrddhānamavajighrati \ prajāpateṣūvā hiṃkāreṇāvajighrāmi sahasrāyuṣāsau jīva śaradaḥ śatamiti
children.translated_text: Then he smells his head: "As <s>Prajāpati</s>, with the hiṃkāra, I smell you. O such-and-such, live a hundred autumns with a life of a thousand years."
And three times, "With the hiṃkāra of the cows I smell you."

children.text: dakṣiṇe 'sya karṇe japati \ asme prayandhi maghavannṛjīṣinnindrarāyoviśvavārasya bhūreḥ \ asme śataṃ śarado jīvase dhā asmai vīrāñcchaśvata indra śiprinniti
children.translated_text: In his right ear he murmurs: "Grant to us, O bountiful <s>Maghavan</s>, O vigorous <s>Indra</s>, much wealth that wins every prize. For him establish a hundred autumns to live; for him, O <s>Indra Śiprin</s>, grant lasting heroes."

children.text: indra śreṣūhāni draviṇāni dhehi cittiṃ dakṣasya subhagatvamasme \ poṣaṃ rayīṇāmariṣūiṃ tanūnāṃ svātmānaṃ vācaḥ sudinatvamahnāmiti savye
children.translated_text: In the left ear: "O <s>Indra</s>, bestow the best treasures, insight, skill, and good fortune upon us; nourishment of riches, soundness of bodies, self-possession, speech, and good days."
For a girl, however, he only smells the head silently.
In the sixth month is the annaprāśana, the first feeding of solid food.

children.text: sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvājyabhāgāviṣūvājyāhutī juhoti devīṃ vācamajanayanta devāstāṃ viśvarūpāḥ paśavo vadanti \ sā no mandreṣamūrjaṃ duhānā dhenurvāgasmānupasuṣūutaitu svāheti
children.translated_text: After cooking a sthālīpāka, he offers the two portions of ghee and the intervening ghee-offerings: "The gods generated the goddess Speech; animals of every form speak her. May she, a cow giving milk of sweetness and strength, come near to us, svāhā."
And the second oblation is with the verse beginning, "May strength be ours today."

children.text: sthālīpākasya juhoti prāṇenānnamaśīya svāhāpānena gandhānaśīya svāhā cakṣuṣā rūpāṇyaśīya svāhā śrotreṇa yaśo 'śīya svāheti
children.translated_text: He offers from the sthālīpāka: "By prāṇa may I eat food, svāhā. By apāna may I enjoy fragrances, svāhā. By sight may I enjoy forms, svāhā. By hearing may I enjoy fame, svāhā."
At the end of the offerings, having taken out together all flavors and all kinds of food, he should then make the child eat.

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ hanteti vā hantakāraṃ manuṣyā iti śruteḥ
children.translated_text: Silently, or saying "hanta," because scripture says, "The hanta-call belongs to men."
For one who desires eloquence, he feeds him with the meat of a bhāradvājī bird.
For one who desires the eating of food, with the meat of a kapiñjala bird.
For one who desires speed, with fish.
For one who desires long life, with kṛkaṣā.
For one who desires brahmanical brilliance, with ājya, clarified butter.
For one who desires all things, with all of them.

children.text: anna paryāya vā tato brāhmaṇabhojanamannaparyāya vā tato brāhmaṇabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: Or a course of food; after that, feeding of brāhmaṇas. Or a course of food; after that, feeding of brāhmaṇas.

children.text: catvāraḥ pākayajñā huto 'hutaḥ prahutaḥ prāśita iti ||
children.translated_text: There are four pākayajñas: offered in the fire, not offered in the fire, offered forth, and eaten.

children.text: pañcasu bahiḥ śālāyāṃ vivāhe cūḍākaraṇa upanayane keśānte sīmantonnayana iti ||
children.translated_text: On five occasions they are performed outside the hall: at marriage, tonsure, initiation, the keśānta, and the sīmantonnayana.
On a smeared, raised, and sprinkled place he sets up the fire.
Some say that at marriage the fire should be produced by churning.

children.text: udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇyāhe kumāryāḥ pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: In the northern course of the sun, in the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious day, he should take the maiden's hand.
On each of the three, beginning with the one after the three.
Under <s>Svātī</s>, under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, or under <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
For a brāhmaṇa there are three women, in the order of the varṇas.
For a rājanya, two.
For a vaiśya, one.
For all of them, some allow even a śūdra woman, but without mantras.

children.text: athaināṃ vāsaḥ paridhāpayati jarāṃ gaccha paridhatsva vāso bhavākṛṣṭīnām abhiśastipāvā
children.translated_text: Then he makes her put on a garment: "Go to old age; put on the garment. Be one who wipes away curses for those who draw you on.

children.text: śataṃ ca jīva śaradaḥ suvarccā rayiṃ ca putrān anusaṃvyayasvāyuṣmatīdaṃ paridhatsva vāsa iti ||
children.translated_text: Live a hundred autumns, radiant; and obtain wealth and sons. Long-lived, put on this garment."
Then the upper garment.
"Those who cut, who wove, who stretched it out,

children.text: yāś ca devīs tantūn abhito tatantha
children.translated_text: and the goddesses who spread the threads on every side,

children.text: tās tvā devīr jarase saṃvyayasvāyuṣmatīdaṃ paridhatsva vāsa iti ||
children.translated_text: may those goddesses clothe you for old age. Long-lived, put on this garment."
Then he anoints the two together.

children.text: samañjantu viśvedevāḥ sam āpo hṛdayāni nau
children.translated_text: "May all the gods unite us; may the waters unite our hearts,

children.text: saṃ mātariśvā saṃdhātā sam u deṣṭrī dadhātu nāv iti ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Mātariśvan</s>, may the arranger, and may the instructor unite us both."
Having taken her, given by her father, he takes hold of her and goes out.

children.text: yad aiṣi manasā dūraṃ diśo 'nu pavamāno vā
children.translated_text: "When you go far away with your mind, along the directions, or as the purifying wind,

children.text: hiraṇyaparṇo vaikarṇaḥ sa tvā manmanasāṃ karotv ity asāv iti ||
children.translated_text: may the golden-winged, wide-eared one make you of my mind." He adds her name.
Then he makes the two look at each other.

children.text: aghoracakṣur apatighny edhi śivā paśubhyaḥ sumanāḥ suvarccāḥ
children.translated_text: "Be one whose eye is not terrible, not husband-slaying; be auspicious to cattle, kindly, radiant,

children.text: vīrasūr devakāmā syonā śan no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade
children.translated_text: a mother of heroes, devoted to the gods, pleasant. Be welfare for our bipeds and welfare for our quadrupeds.

children.text: somaḥ prathamo vivide gandharvo vivida uttaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> was the first to find you; the <s>Gandharva</s> found you next.

children.text: tṛtīyo 'gniṣṭe patis turīyas te manuṣyajāḥ somo 'dadad gandharvāya gandharvo 'dadad agnaye
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> was your third husband; the fourth is one born among men. <s>Soma</s> gave you to the <s>Gandharva</s>, the <s>Gandharva</s> gave you to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: rayiṃ ca putrāṃś cādād agnir mahyam atho imām
children.translated_text: And <s>Agni</s> has given wealth and sons, and then this woman, to me.

children.text: sā naḥ pūṣā śivatamām airaya sā na ūrū uśatī vihara
children.translated_text: May <s>Pūṣan</s> send her to us most auspicious; may she, desiring us, spread her thighs for us,

children.text: yasyām uśantaḥ praharāma śepaṃ yasyām u kāmā bahavo niviṣṭyā iti ||
children.translated_text: she in whom, desirous, we place the male member, she in whom many desires are set."
Some lead them around the fire clockwise.

children.text: paścād agnes tejanīṃ kaṭaṃ vā dakṣiṇapādena pravṛtyopaviśati ||
children.translated_text: Behind the fire, having stepped with her right foot onto a mat or a reed seat, she sits down.

children.text: anvārabdha āghārāv ājyabhāgau mahāvyāhṛtayaḥ sarvaprāyaścittaṃ prājāpatyaṃ sviṣṭakṛc ca ||
children.translated_text: While she is touching him from behind, there are the two āghāra offerings, the two portions of ghee, the great utterances, the all-expiation, the Prajāpati oblation, and the sviṣṭakṛt.
This is regular everywhere.

children.text: prāṅ mahāvyāhṛtibhyaḥ sviṣṭakṛd anyac ced ājyāddhaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the oblation is something other than ghee, the sviṣṭakṛt comes before the great utterances.
In the marriage rite this is the insertion point, after the all-expiation and before the Prajāpati oblation.
If he wishes, and if he knows them, he offers the Rāṣṭrabhṛt offerings and the Jayā and Abhyātāna formulas.
Because of the statement, "By which rite he prospers."

children.text: cittaṃ ca cittiś cākūtaṃ cākūtiś ca vijñātaṃ ca vijñātiś ca manaś ca śakvarīś ca darśaś ca paurṇamāsaṃ ca bṛhac ca rathantaraṃ ca
children.translated_text: "Thought and thinking, intention and intending, what is known and knowing, mind and the Śakvarī verses, new moon and full moon, the <s>Bṛhat</s> and the <s>Rathantara</s>.

children.text: prajāpatir jayān indrāya vṛṣṇe prāyacchad ugraḥ pṛtanā jayeṣu
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, fierce, gave the victory-formulas to mighty <s>Indra</s> in the battles for victory.

children.text: tasmai viśaḥ samanamanta sarvāḥ sa ugraḥ sa ihavyo babhūva svāheti ||
children.translated_text: To him all the peoples bowed together; he became fierce and worthy of invocation here. Svāhā."

children.text: agnir bhūtānām adhipatiḥ samāvatv indro jyeṣṭhānāṃ yamaḥ pṛthivyā vāyur antarikṣasya sūryo divaś candramā nakṣatrāṇāṃ bṛhaspatir brahmaṇo mitraḥ satyānāṃ varuṇo 'pāṃ samudraḥ srotyānām annaṃ sāmrājyānām adhipati tanmāvatu soma oṣadhīnāṃ savitā prasavānāṃ rudraḥ paśūnāṃ tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāṃ viṣṇuḥ parvatānāṃ maruto gaṇānām adhipatayas te māvantu pitaraḥ pitāmahāḥ parevare tatāstatāmahāḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Agni</s>, lord of beings, protect me; <s>Indra</s> of the eldest, <s>Yama</s> of the earth, <s>Vāyu</s> of the midspace, <s>Sūrya</s> of heaven, the moon of the asterisms, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> of brahman, <s>Mitra</s> of truths, <s>Varuṇa</s> of the waters, the ocean of streams, food as lord of sovereignties: may that protect me. <s>Soma</s> of herbs, <s>Savitṛ</s> of impellings, <s>Rudra</s> of cattle, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> of forms, <s>Viṣṇu</s> of mountains, the <s>Maruts</s> of hosts: may those lords protect me. May the fathers, grandfathers, and earlier and later ancestors, the fathers' fathers,

children.text: iha māvantv asmin brahmaṇy asmin kṣatre 'syām āśiṣyasyāṃ purodhāyām asmin karmaṇy asyāṃ devahūtyāṃ svāheti sarvatrānuṣajati ||
children.translated_text: protect me here, in this brahman, in this kṣatra, in this blessing, in this priestly office, in this rite, in this invocation of the gods. Svāhā"; he appends this everywhere.

children.text: agnir aitu prathamo devatānāṃ so 'syai prajāṃ muñcatu mṛtyupāśāt
children.translated_text: "Let <s>Agni</s>, first of the deities, come; may he release offspring for her from the snare of death.

children.text: tad ayaṃ rājā varuṇo 'num anyatāṃ yatheyaṃ strī pautramaghannarodāt svāhā
children.translated_text: May this king <s>Varuṇa</s> approve it, so that this woman may not weep from lack of grandsons. Svāhā.

children.text: imām agnis trāyatāṅgārhapatyaḥ prajām asyai nayatu dīrgham āyuḥ
children.translated_text: May this <s>Agni</s> Gārhapatya protect her; may he lead offspring and long life to her.

children.text: aśūnyopasthā jīvatām astu mātā pautram ānandam abhivibudhyatām iyaṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: May she be a mother whose lap is not empty, living; may this woman awaken to the joy of a grandson. Svāhā.

children.text: svastino agne diva āpṛthivyā viśvānidhehyayathā yajatra yad asyāṃ mahidivi jātaṃ praśastaṃ tad asmāsu draviṇaṃ dhehi citraṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: Grant us well-being, O <s>Agni</s>, from heaven and earth; place all treasures here for us, O worthy of sacrifice. Whatever excellent thing has arisen in this great heaven, place that splendid wealth among us. Svāhā.

children.text: sugannu panthāṃ pradiśan na ehi jyotiṣmadhye hyajaran na āyuḥ
children.translated_text: Come to us, showing an easy path; enter the midst of light, bringing ageless life to us.

children.text: apaitu mṛtyur amṛtanna āgād vaivasvato no abhayaṃ kṛṇotu svāheti ||
children.translated_text: Let death go away; immortality has come to us. May <s>Vaivasvata</s> make fearlessness for us. Svāhā."
And some add the verse beginning "Away to death" after the eating.

children.text: kumāryā bhrātā śamīpalāśamiśrāṃl lājān añjalināñjalāv āvapati ||
children.translated_text: The brother of the maiden pours parched grain mixed with leaves of śamī and palāśa from joined handfuls into her joined hands.

children.text: tāñ juhoti saṃhatena tiṣṭhatī aryamaṇaṃ devaṃ kanyāgnim ayakṣata
children.translated_text: She offers them, standing with her hands joined: "The maiden has sacrificed to the god <s>Aryaman</s>, to the fire of the bride.

children.text: sano aryamā devaḥ preto muñcatu mā pateḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: May that god <s>Aryaman</s>, when he has gone forth, release us, not from the husband. Svāhā.
This woman says nearby, as she pours in the parched grains:

children.text: āyuṣmān astu me patir edhantāṃ jñātayo mama svāhā
children.translated_text: May my husband be long-lived; may my kinsmen prosper. Svāhā.

children.text: imāṃl lājān āvapāmy agnau samṛddhikaraṇaṃ tava
children.translated_text: I pour these parched grains into the fire, for the making of your prosperity.

children.text: mama tubhyaṃ ca saṃvananaṃ tad agnir anumanyatām iyaṃ svāheti ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Agni</s> approve that union of me and you. This woman, svāhā."

children.text: athāsyai dakṣiṇaṃ hastam gṛhṇāti sāṅguṣṭhaṃ gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ mayāpatyā jaradaṣṭir yathā saḥ
children.translated_text: Then he takes her right hand, including the thumb: "I take your hand for good fortune, so that with me as husband you may reach old age.

children.text: bhago 'ryamā savitā purandhir mahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya devāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, and <s>Purandhi</s>: the gods have given you to me for householdership.

children.text: amo 'ham asmi sā tvaṃ sā tvam asy amo 'ham
children.translated_text: I am he; you are she. You are she; I am he.

children.text: sāmāham asmi ṛk tvaṃ dyaur ahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ tāv ehi vivahāvahai sahareto dadhāvahai prajāṃ prajanayāvahai putrān vindyāvahai bahūn te santu jaradaṣṭayaḥ saṃpriyau rociṣṇū sumanasyamānau paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ śataṃ śṛṇuyāma śaradaḥ śatam iti ||
children.translated_text: "I am the Sāman, you are the Ṛc; I am heaven, you are earth. Come, let us two marry; let us join seed together; let us beget offspring; let us obtain many sons. May they live to old age. Loving one another, shining, well-disposed in mind, may we see a hundred autumns, may we live a hundred autumns, may we hear a hundred autumns."

children.text: athainām aśmānam ārohayaty uttarato 'gner dakṣiṇapādena ārohemam aśmānam aśmeva tvaṃ sthirā bhava
children.translated_text: Then he makes her mount a stone to the north of the fire with her right foot: "Mount this stone; like a stone, be firm.
Stand against those who attack; drive away the hostile ones."

children.text: atha gāthāṃ gāyati sarasvati predamava subhage vājinīvatī
children.translated_text: Then he sings a gāthā: "O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, come forward here, blessed one, rich in strength,

children.text: yāṃ tvā viśvasya bhūtasya prajāyām asyāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: you whom, at the foremost place, he has set over the offspring of this whole created world,

children.text: yasyāṃ bhūtaṃ samabhavad yasyāṃ viśvam idaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: in whom created being came into existence, in whom this whole world exists.

children.text: tām adya gāthāṃ gāsyāmi yā strīṇām uttamaṃ yaśa iti ||
children.translated_text: Today I shall sing that gāthā which is the highest fame of women."

children.text: atha parikrāmataḥ tubhyam agre paryavahan sūryāṃ vahatu nā saha
children.translated_text: Then the two go around: "Beforehand they led <s>Sūryā</s> around for you; may <s>Vahatu</s> not lead her away with him.

children.text: punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṃ dāgne prajayā saheti ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, give back the wife to her husbands together with offspring."
In this way, twice more, the lājā offering and the rest are performed.

children.text: caturthaṃ śūrpakuṣṭhayā sarvāṃl lājān āvapati bhagāya svāheti ||
children.translated_text: A fourth time, with the corner of the winnowing basket, he pours all the parched grain in, saying, "To <s>Bhaga</s>, svāhā."
After she has been led around three times, he offers the oblation to <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: athainām udīcīṃ saptapadāni prakrāmayati ekam iṣe dve ūrje trīṇi rāyaspoṣāya catvāri māyobhavāya pañca paśubhyaḥ ṣaḍ ṛtubhyaḥ sakhe saptapadā bhava sā mām anuvratā bhava ||
children.translated_text: Then he makes her take seven steps northward: "One for nourishment, two for strength, three for prosperity in wealth, four for well-being, five for cattle, six for the seasons. Friend, be one who has taken seven steps; be devoted to me."
Everywhere he appends, "May <s>Viṣṇu</s> lead you."

children.text: niṣkramaṇaprabhṛtyudakumbhaṃ skandhe kṛtvā dakṣiṇato 'gner vāgyataḥ sthito bhavati ||
children.translated_text: From the departure onward, carrying a water jar on his shoulder, he stands silently to the south of the fire.
According to some, to the north.

children.text: tata enāṃ mūrddhany abhiṣiñcati āpaḥ śivāḥ śivatamāḥ śāntāḥ śāntatamās tās te kṛṇvantu bheṣajam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he sprinkles her on the head: "Waters, auspicious, most auspicious, peaceful, most peaceful, may you make medicine for her."
And with the three verses beginning "You waters are best."

children.text: athaināṃ sūryam udīkṣayati tac cakṣur iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he makes her look up at the sun with the formula beginning "That eye."

children.text: athāsyai dakṣiṇāṃ samadhi hṛdayam ālabhate mama vrate te hṛdayaṃ dadhāmi mama cittam anucittaṃ te astu mama vācam ekamanā juṣasva prajāpatiṣ ṭvā niyunaktu mahyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he touches her right side near the heart: "I place your heart in my vow. Let your mind be in accord with my mind. With one mind accept my speech. May <s>Prajāpati</s> assign you to me."

children.text: athainām abhimantrayate sumaṅgalīr iyam vadhūr imāṃ sameta paśyata saubhāgyam asyai datvāyāthāstaṃ viparetaneti ||
children.translated_text: Then he addresses her: "This bride is auspicious; come together and look at her. Having given her good fortune, go back to your own homes."

children.text: tāṃ dṛḍhapuruṣa unmathya prāgvodagvānugupta āgāra ānaḍuhe rohite carmaṇy upaveśayati iha gāvo niṣīdantv ihāśvā iha pūruṣāḥ
children.translated_text: A strong man, lifting her firmly, seats her in a protected house facing east or north on the hide of a red bull: "Here let the cows sit; here the horses; here the men.

children.text: iho sahasradakṣiṇo yajña iha pūṣā niṣīdantv iti ||
children.translated_text: Here let the sacrifice with a thousand gifts, here let <s>Pūṣan</s>, sit."
They should also make a village pronouncement.
Because of the statement, "At a marriage and at a funeral one should enter the village."

children.text: tasmāt tayor grāmaḥ pramānam iti śruteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the village is the authority for those two, according to revelation.
He gives a boon to the teacher.
A cow is the boon for a brāhmaṇa.
A village is the boon for a kṣatriya.
A horse is the boon for a vaiśya.
A hundred on the chariot is given to the man who has a daughter.
When the sun has set, he shows her the fixed star <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: dhruvam asi dhruvaṃ tvā paśyāmi dhruvaidhipoṣye mayi mahyaṃ tvādādabṛhaspatim aryā patyā prajāvatī saṃjīva śaradaḥ śatam iti ||
children.translated_text: "You are fixed; I see you as fixed. Be fixed for prosperity in me. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> has given you to me; living with a noble husband and with offspring, live a hundred autumns."

children.text: sā yadi na paśyet paśyāmīty eva brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: If she does not see it, she should still say, "I see it."

children.text: trirātram akṣārālavaṇāśinau syātām adhaḥ śayīyātāṃ saṃvatsaraṃ na mithunam upeyātāṃ dvādaśarātraṃ ṣaḍrātraṃ trirātram antataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For three nights the two should eat without alkali and salt; they should sleep on the ground. For a year they should not approach each other sexually; or for twelve nights, six nights, or at least three nights.
From the marriage onward, there is attendance on the domestic fire.
At sunset and sunrise, with curds, rice grains, or unbroken grains.
In the evening: "To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā; to <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā."
In the morning: "To <s>Sūrya</s>, svāhā; to <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā."

children.text: pumāṃsau mitrāvaruṇau pumāṃsāv aśvināv ubhau pumān indraś ca sūryaś ca pumāṃsaṃ vartatāṃ mayi punaḥ svāheti pūrvāṃ garbhakāmā ||
children.translated_text: If she desires a male child, she first offers: "The two <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> are male; both <s>Aśvins</s> are male; <s>Indra</s> and <s>Sūrya</s> are male; may a male turn toward me again, svāhā."

children.text: rājño 'kṣabhede naddhavimokṣe yānaviparyāse 'nyasyāṃ vā vyāpattau striyāś codvahane tam evāgnim upasamādhāyājyaṃ saṃskṛtyeharatir iti juhoti nānāmantrābhyām ||
children.translated_text: If a king's axle breaks, if a binding is loosened, if a vehicle overturns, in some other mishap, or in the taking of a woman in marriage, he sets up that same fire, prepares the ghee, and offers with the two different mantras beginning "Here is delight."

children.text: anyad yānam upakalpya tatropaveśayedrājānaṃ striyaṃ vā pratikṣatra iti yajñāntenātvāhārṣam iti caitayā ||
children.translated_text: Having prepared another vehicle, he should seat the king or the woman in it, with the formula beginning "Against hostile power," and with the verse "I have brought you here" at the end of the sacrifice.
The two draught animals are the fee.
This is the expiation.
After that comes the feeding of brāhmaṇas.

children.text: caturthyām apararātre 'bhyantarato 'gnim upasamādhāya dakṣiṇato brahmāṇam upaveśyottarata udapātraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvājyabhāgāv iṣṭvājyāhutīr juhoti ||
children.translated_text: On the fourth night, in the latter part of the night, he sets up the fire inside, seats the <s>brahman</s> priest to the south, places a water vessel to the north, cooks a mess of boiled rice, offers the two ghee portions, and makes the intervening ghee-offerings.

children.text: agne prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇas tvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai patighnī tanūs tām asyai nāśaya svāhā
children.translated_text: "O <s>Agni</s> of expiation, you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection I approach you. Destroy for her that body of hers which kills a husband, svāhā.

children.text: vāyo prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇas tvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai prajāghnī tanūs tām asyai nāśaya svāhā
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāyu</s> of expiation, you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection I approach you. Destroy for her that body of hers which kills offspring, svāhā."

children.text: sūryaprāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇas tvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai paśughnī tanūs tām asyai nāśaya svāhā
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūrya</s> of expiation, you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection I approach you. Destroy for her that body of hers which kills cattle, svāhā.

children.text: candra prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇas tvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai gṛhaghnī tanūs tām asyai nāśaya svāhā
children.translated_text: O <s>Candra</s> of expiation, you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection I approach you. Destroy for her that body of hers which kills the house, svāhā.

children.text: gandharva prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇas tvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai yaśoghnī tanūs tām asyai nāśaya svāheti ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Gandharva</s> of expiation, you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection I approach you. Destroy for her that body of hers which kills fame, svāhā.
He makes an offering from the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (boiled rice mess), saying, "To <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā."

children.text: hutvā hutvaitāsām āhutīnām udapātre saṃsravānt samavanīya tata enāṃ mūrddhany abhiṣiñcati
children.translated_text: Having offered each of these oblations, he pours the run-off into the water vessel; then he sprinkles her on the head.

children.text: yāte patighnī prajāghnī paśughnī gṛhaghnī yaśoghnī ninditā tanūr jāraghnīṃ tata enāṃ karomi sā jīrya tvaṃ mayā sahāsāv iti ||
children.translated_text: "That censured body of yours which kills a husband, kills offspring, kills cattle, kills the house, kills fame, and kills a lover: from that I make her freed. Grow old together with me, O such-and-such."

children.text: athaināṃ sthālīpākaṃ prāśayati prāṇais te prāṇānt saṃdadhābhyasthibhir asthīni māṃsair māṃsāni tvacā tvacam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he makes her eat the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (boiled rice mess), saying, "With the breaths I join your breaths, with the bones your bones, with the flesh your flesh, with the skin your skin."

children.text: tasmād evaṃvicchrotriyasya dāreṇa nopahāsam icched uta hy evaṃvitparo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one who knows this should not seek jesting with the wife of a learned <s>śrotriya</s>; for one who knows this becomes superior.
Having married her, the entry is made at the proper season.
Or, as one desires, according to the statement, "There is intercourse at will until conception."
Then he touches her right side, near the heart.

children.text: yat te susīme hṛdayaṃ divi candramasi śritam
children.translated_text: "That heart of yours, O well-parted one, which rests in heaven, in the moon:

children.text: vedāhaṃ tan māṃ tad vidyāt paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ śataṃ śṛṇuyāma śaradaḥ śatam iti ||
children.translated_text: I know it; may it know me. May we see a hundred autumns, may we live a hundred autumns, may we hear a hundred autumns."
In this same way thereafter.
